Bra Fitting Guide

Article 2 — Cups: Size, Shape, and Spillage

Most cup problems come from wrong volume or wrong shape for your breast type.

Reviewed by the Breast Calculator Editorial Team · Published June 17, 2026 · 5 min read

2.1 Gaping, Wrinkled, or Collapsed Cups (#04)

Root causes: Cup volume> actual tissue; breast shape is full-on-bottom or teardrop; closed upper cup.

Core fixes: Try one cup size smaller. Switch to a balconette, demi, or half-cup style. Molded T-shirt bras work well for shallow shapes.

2.2 Quad-Boob / Top Spillage (#05)

Root cause: Cup too small (most common). Also temporary hormonal swelling.

Core fixes: Go up one or two cup sizes. Choose seamed or full-coverage styles that encapsulate rather than compress. Keep a larger wireless bra for period days.

2.3 Side Spillage / Armpit Bulge (#06)

Root cause: Cup too narrow → breast tissue pushed sideways. Weak side wings.

Core fixes: Go up one cup. Look for "high-wing" or "side-support" construction. Always scoop and swoop when putting on a bra.

2.4 Falling Out When Leaning Forward (#14)

Root cause: Cups too shallow, too small, or wrong shape.

Core fixes: Go up one cup and choose full-coverage or balconette with strong side panels. For projected breasts, look for deeper cup styles.

Bottom line: Cup problems are rarely about "being too big" or "too small" — they are about matching your breast volume and shape to the right cut. Continue to Article 3 — The Band .

Bra Size Comparisons

Now that you understand sister sizes, explore our detailed side-by-side size comparisons to see the real differences in cup volume, band support, and fit.

32D vs 34C

Sister sizes with ~420 cc each. Find the right balance between band snugness and comfort.

34B vs 36C

Different cup volumes — 350 cc vs 450 cc. Understand which matches your measurements.

36B vs 34C

Classic sister size trade-off: larger band + smaller cup, or smaller band + larger cup.

34DD vs 36D

Fuller bust comparison with ~700 cc each. Support and comfort for DD/D cups.

38C vs 40B

Plus size sister sizes with ~480 cc each. Band comfort and support balance.

B Cup vs C Cup

The most common cup size confusion — see the 1-inch difference in volume.

C Cup vs D Cup

More volume, more projection, and different bra needs for each size.

D Cup vs DD Cup

Where support needs change dramatically between sizes.

DD Cup vs DDD Cup

The DD-to-DDD gap — professional fitting often reveals surprises here.

Wireless vs Wired Bra

Not a cup comparison — style choice for breast shape and daily comfort.
